summary: Ephemeral sidecar connection throttle causing reserved pool throughput sink during midday window
description:
Issue summary:
During the midday traffic window (11:30–13:00 UTC) LexiAI observed a sustained drop in reserved pool throughput for their dedicated capacity in us-east-1. P95 token latency for generation routes rose from baseline ~180ms to 3.8–5.2s and effective GPU throughput (tokens/sec) declined by ~34% for 35 minutes.

Impact:
- Customer-facing generation latency and throughput regression for all pinned routes using open-34b-v2 and redwood/opt-12b.
- Requests succeeded after retries but experienced higher cost and degraded SLAs.
- No model code change on customer side; traffic pattern consistent.

Environment:
- Customer tier: dedicated (reserved capacity).
- Region: prod | us-east-1.
- Affected pool: reserved-pool-lexiai-us-east-1 (4x A100s).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Midday steady-state traffic with many short-lived streams (chatlets with 1–3 messages).
2) Sidecar shard processes emit clustered healthcheck sweeps and connection resets when ephemeral sidecars rotate.
3) Serving allocator begins to see increased attach latencies and transient attach failures (~10–15% attach error rate).
4) Autoscaler interprets attach delays as reduced capacity and briefly throttles new slots, causing queued requests and p95 latency surge.

Observed telemetry & logs (high-level):
- p95 latency spike: 180ms -> 3.8–5.2s (11:41–12:16 UTC).
- GPU attach latency (median): 40ms -> 420ms; attach failures increased from 0.3% -> 12%.
- Sidecar connection churn: 600 conn/s -> 2,900 conn/s during rotation bursts.
- Kernel-level NVLINK and PCIe I/O did not show sustained saturation.

Representative log excerpts (redacted):
- \"sidecar/rotate: flushing idle connections; purge_count=312; sweep_time=82ms\"
- \"allocator: attach_timeout for tenant=lexiai; attempt=3; err=attach_backoff\"
- \"autoscaler: pool_shrink_decision -> temporary_throttle, reason=attach_latency_polling\"

Notes: initial alert routing triggered support P1 due to dedicated SLA exposure and visible customer impact.
comments: 2026-03-12 11:55 — Avery Chen (Support): Customer reports p95 jump and throughput loss. Collected traces, request IDs, and pool name. Escalating to SRE.

2026-03-12 12:05 — Diego Morales (SRE): Observed attach latency spike for reserved-pool-lexiai-us-east-1. Sidecar rotation pattern aligns with spikes. Hypothesis: sidecar connection churn causing allocator to hit backoff heuristics.

2026-03-12 12:18 — LexiAI CCR (Customer): Confirmed no deployment change. Traffic pattern unchanged but we did see increased short-lived message bursts from a scheduled campaign. Asking for mitigation to meet SLAs.

2026-03-12 12:38 — Priya Rao (Runtime Eng): Reproduced attach timeouts in staging by simulating repeated sidecar reconnects. Candidate fix: increase allocator attach window and add smoothing for autoscaler feed; separate patch to limit sidecar sweep concurrency.

2026-03-13 09:12 — Diego Morales (SRE): Deployed emergency autoscaler smoothing (hotfix) to reserved pool; immediate p95 improvement to ~220ms and attach failure rate dropped to <1%. Monitoring for 48h. Customer notified of mitigation.
2026-03-13 11:45 — LexiAI CCR (Customer): Reports improved latency and throughput after the hotfix. Requesting postmortem and permanent fix timeline.
investigation_notes: Confirmed correlation between sidecar rotation events and attach latency spikes using trace IDs and connection metrics.
Allocator backoff heuristics were tripping on transient attach failures; these heuristics are aggressive for reserved pools under certain failure patterns.
Autoscaler used attach-latency signal in decision loop; noisy attach signal led to unnecessary short-term throttles.
No evidence of GPU-level resource exhaustion (mem/cache stable); issue is scheduling/attach signal amplification.
Staging reproduction shows same behavior when simulating 2.5–3x normal connection churn during rotation windows.
resolution: Mitigation applied (2026-03-13): rolled a quick autoscaler smoothing hotfix and increased allocator attach window for affected reserved pools. Immediate impact: p95 and attach-failure rates returned near baseline. Next actions: 1) schedule a runtime patch to limit concurrent sidecar sweep concurrency and add jitter to rotation; 2) harden autoscaler decision logic to ignore short-lived attach spikes (tunable window); 3) create a runbook for 'sidecar rotation' signatures to trigger automatic soft-throttles rather than full pool shrink. Owner: Runtime Eng (Priya Rao). Target ETA for permanent fixes: 2026-03-20. Follow-up: postmortem and regression test added to CI for connection-churn scenarios.
next_steps: Apply sidecar sweep concurrency cap and jitter patch (PR referenced above) — runtime team
